title: MACHHUB Data Bridge Import File
description: A single bridge object, an array of bridge objects, or a versioned wrapper. All three are accepted by the Data Bridge import dialog.

version.description: Format version. Omit or set to 1.

name.description: Unique within the environment. Import matches on this to detect a collision.

driver.description: Only MySQL is supported today. The driver sits behind an interface so Postgres and MSSQL can be added without changing this format.

username.description: Not strictly required by the API, but a bridge without one will not connect to MySQL. Always set it.

password.description: NEVER produced by export. Accepted on import for automated setup only; prefer leaving it out and entering the password in the import dialog.

tlsMode.description: "true" verifies the server certificate; "skip-verify" encrypts without verifying; "preferred" uses TLS if the server offers it.

bufferMaxAge.description: How long an undelivered record is kept in the store-and-forward buffer. Overflow drops the oldest first.

bufferMaxBytes.description: Size cap on the buffer, in bytes. Whichever of age or size hits first wins. This is the cap that matters in practice — 72h is only reachable at modest sample rates.

id.description: Required, and unique within the bridge for its direction. A UUID is conventional; any stable string works.

name.description: Human label shown in the UI.

enabled.description: Omit and the route is imported enabled — a route written into a file is one the author wants running.

selector.description: MQTT-style UNS topic selector. '+' matches one level, '#' matches the rest. e.g. "plantA/+/temperature".

table.description: Target table. It must already exist — the bridge never creates tables.

upsertKeys.description: Required when writeMode is "upsert". Every key must also appear as a mapped column AND be covered by a UNIQUE or PRIMARY key on the target table.

enabled.description: Omit and the route is imported enabled — a route written into a file is one the author wants running.

table.description: Source table. Either this or `query` is required.

query.description: Custom SELECT, used instead of `table`. It must expose watermarkCol and take the watermark as a single `?` bind parameter.

watermarkCol.description: Column the poller resumes from. Index it — every poll filters on it.

watermarkKind.description: "autoincrement" is safer: a timestamp watermark can skip rows committed out of order relative to their timestamps, which is what safetyLag exists to mitigate.

safetyLag.description: Timestamp watermarks only. Rows newer than now-safetyLag are left for the next poll so in-flight transactions have committed. Ignored for autoincrement.

topicTemplate.description: UNS topic to publish to. Interpolates row columns with Go template syntax, e.g. "plantA/{{.machine_id}}/status".

payload.description: Which row columns become which payload fields. Omit to publish the whole row.

watermark.description: RUNTIME STATE — never write this in a file. Export strips it, and import drops it: an imported route must start from the beginning rather than skip rows it has never read.

lastPollDt.description: RUNTIME STATE — never write this in a file.

column.description: Target column name (egress) or payload field name (ingress).

source.description: value = the tag value; timestamp = the sample's source time; topic = the full UNS topic; literal = the constant in `expr`; jsonpath = the field of a structured payload at the path in `expr`.

expr.description: Required when source is "literal" (the constant) or "jsonpath" (the path, e.g. "$.motor.rpm"). Ignored otherwise.

type.description: Declared target type. Checked against the real column type at save time, so a narrowing conversion is refused up front rather than truncating on the first drain.

goDuration.description: Go duration string: a number and a unit, optionally repeated. "30s", "72h", "1h30m". NOT "3d" — days are not a Go unit; write "72h".
